subject: DPA: role allocation, encryption safeguards & export-routing questions (MedLynx)
messages:
From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@medlynx.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@medlynx.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Initial redline + controller/processor split questions

Irene — attaching our initial redline on the MSA + proposed DPA annex (MedLynx redline v1). A few immediate questions so we can surface them to procurement/legal: 

1) Controller vs Processor: for the health analytics features we discussed, is Redwood proposing to be a processor for patient data and a controller for telemetry/usage metrics? The current MSA language is mixed and our counsel wants a clear split.

2) Encryption at rest and KMS: we see a note in the DPA about encryption but need concrete text around who holds the keys for customer data vs. operational logs. Are you able to confirm support for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for EU tenants?

3) Cross-border routing: we have concerns about backups and fallbacks triggering a US region; can you confirm whether the service will ever route EU customer data outside EEA without prior notice and SCCs in place?

We included an initial data flow diagram and the suggested language to keep the export path explicitly limited. Attaching: MedLynx_DPA_redline_v1.docx and medlynx-data-flow-2026-11-29.png

Appreciate a quick triage — we are trying to get legal signoff by mid-December.

Best,
Emma
Senior Procurement Manager
MedLynx Health

Attachments: MedLynx_DPA_redline_v1.docx (word), medlynx-data-flow-2026-11-29.png (image)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@medlynx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial redline + controller/processor split questions

Emma — thanks for the redline and the data flow. High level responses below; we'll follow up with tracked redlines and a short call this week to walk both counsels through.

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood will be Processor for customer-provided patient data used by the model inference path. Telemetry/usage metrics collected for platform health are treated as Controller data for Redwood operational purposes; we'll add a definitions table and a short carve-out in the DPA to make that explicit.

2) KMS / CMKs: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers (default) we offer envelope encryption with customer-specific key scoping; we do not currently support BYOK for free-tier hosted instances. For EU tenants under this SOW we can propose a KMS integration clause and show the required permission model.

3) Cross-border routing & backups: Redwood's default is region-local storage for EU tenants. Only under failover (severe outage) would we route to a different region and then only to a compatible EU/legal region or under SCCs+approved addendum. We'll propose explicit language: "Data will not be transferred outside the EEA except as necessary for failover and only under SCCs or Customer instruction; Customer will be notified within X hours".

Can you confirm whether MedLynx needs the stronger "no exports" exception or the soft-failover language above? If they need the former we should discuss operational impacts given our multi-region disaster recovery.

I'll have Ben and Karthik draft a redline for your counters. Propose a 30-minute call Wed 10:00 CET to walk counsel through the skeleton.

Thanks,
Irene
Sr. Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:48:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: draft redline notes for MedLynx DPA

Team — I reviewed Emma's redline and sketched comments in the attached. Key points for our response: 

- Add a short annex (Export Impact Addendum) that describes acceptable fallback regions and the notification SLA; propose 24-48 hour notification for failover exports.
- For controller/processor clarity: add a definitions table plus Examples-of-Processing appendix (helps sales and PSC).
- SCCs: MedLynx attached SCCs_2024_Annex.pdf; confirm version and whether their legal insists on controller-to-controller routing for certain telemetry. We should preserve our standard vendor-subprocessor clause but allow customer-approved subprocessor list with 30-day notice.
- Encryption: offer a KMS integration plan in the Order Form as an optional line item (DevOps implementation estimate + cost). For Hosted EU customers propose an operational control to keep keys region-scoped and rotate per-customer schedule.

I've attached Ben_MedLynx_DPA_notes.docx with inline comments and a draft of the export language. Laura—can you advise on how aggressive we want the notification SLA (24h vs 72h) from a legal/ops standpoint?

Attachments: Ben_MedLynx_DPA_notes.docx (word), SCCs_2024_Annex.pdf (pdf)
From: Legal Ops <legalops@medlynx.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@medlynx.com>, Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@procurecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial redline + controller/processor split questions

Irene/Ben — thanks for the quick replies. A few clarifications from our side after internal review: 

- MedLynx counsel would prefer the "no exports unless instructed by Customer" language, but they understand DR implications. Their ask is that any failover export be limited to an EU jurisdiction and require pre-agreed SCCs + written notice within 48 hours.
- Regarding KMS: they are willing to accept Redwood-hosted keys provided the keys are region-scoped and we commit to a documented KMS controls checklist (rotation, access audits). They flagged BYOK as preferred but not mandatory.
- Subprocessors: they want a guaranteed 30-day prior notice and an option to review high-risk subprocessors; standard approval will be automatic unless Customer objects within 30 days.

We uploaded a slightly updated data-flow map and a redline that highlights the export passage. Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-medlynx-dpa

Can Redwood produce the draft Export Impact Addendum + KMS implementation line item by EOD Monday 6 Dec? We have a procurement cutoff for inclusion in Q4 contracting.

Regards,
Legal Ops
MedLynx Health

Attachments: medlynx-data-flow-2026-11-29.png (image)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Action plan: MedLynx DPA / Export Addendum / KMS item (next steps)

Team — summary and owners, per MedLynx ask and Legal Ops timeline: 

1) Export Impact Addendum (owner: Ben) — draft a short addendum that limits failover exports to EU jurisdictions, requires SCCs and written notice within 48 hours, and includes a brief list of fallback regions we can support. Deliverable: draft PDF + redline to MedLynx by COB Monday 13 Dec.

2) KMS implementation clause and Order Form line item (owner: Karthik) — produce language describing region-scoped keys for Hosted EU tenants, an implementation estimate (2-3 sprints), and a controls checklist (rotation, audit logs). If MedLynx chooses BYOK call out pricing and dev timeline. Deliverable: draft language + ballpark cost by Friday 10 Dec.

3) Subprocessor notice flow (owner: Laura) — confirm we keep 30-day prior notice, and propose "auto-approve unless Customer objects" with a Customer high-risk review path. Deliverable: confirmation and suggested wording by Thu 9 Dec.

I'll take the meeting invite loop with MedLynx for Wed 10:00 CET. Please add any items I missed.

Thanks,
Irene
Sr. Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
